screen: Quiz question – select the correct meaning
layout: Hero is a single character illustration with a speech-bubble word, the prompt sits as a short line above it, and the answer options are one plain stacked list below, with the progress bar pinned full-width at the very top and skip/check actions anchored at the very bottom.
take: Copy the one-image, one-question, one-option-list structure with all chrome (progress, actions) pushed to the screen edges so the center stays empty and glanceable.

screen: Quiz question with inline correct/incorrect marking
layout: The question itself is the largest element at the top of a narrow card, three answer rows stack directly beneath it, and feedback is shown only as a colored border + check/cross icon on the selected and correct rows plus a one-line hint, with alphabet-style progress dashes above the card.
take: Show right/wrong feedback by recoloring the existing option row instead of adding banners or separate feedback panels.

layout: A short title and one-line description sit above a single horizontal A-Z letter bar that doubles as navigation, with terms grouped under large letter headers and each row reduced to term name, one metadata line, and a single Follow button.
take: Use one persistent horizontal letter scrubber as the only navigation and cap each glossary row to a term plus one line of detail and one action.

layout: The selected letter is highlighted in the top A-Z bar and repeated as a large section heading, with entries below laid out as plain multi-column text lists with no icons, images, or extra UI.
take: Restate the active letter as a big heading for orientation, and strip entry rows down to text only so nothing competes for attention.
